propositions: The per-test hang budget was lowered from 300s to 20s in commit 6a5c88027c5, placing it inside the band of legitimate test costs (18.7–29.93s) measured on the gating coverage leg, causing worker deaths on every CI run.

timeout_method=thread expresses a timeout as os._exit(1) (killing the xdist worker) rather than as a pytest verdict, so budget expiry never produces 'Failed: Timeout' lines and manifests instead as '[gwN] node down: Not properly terminated'.

The first fix (change 2115) failed its own Verified gate because GitHub resolves reusable workflow files from the caller's trusted-main commit, so patchset-side workflow edits to override the budget are inert — the gate executed main's stale --timeout=20 CLI flag, which overrides ini via pytest-timeout precedence.

Restoring timeout=300 to pyproject.toml and both shared-tier _build-and-test.yml lanes, with headroom contract tests, unblocked CI; post-merge Verified runs at a42a9d8d494 show zero worker crashes where pre-fix runs failed.

Under --dist loadgroup, a dead worker re-dispatches its pending work to respawned workers that crash on the same item up to numprocesses*4 restarts, burning toward the 60-min job ceiling (fixed by follow-up 8a4f via --max-worker-restart=0).

The regression was caused by story 73b8-2d79-3046-44ce: a budget calibrated against a fast local unit-tier run without coverage did not account for the 2x coverage multiplier and full-suite contention on the ubuntu-latest leg that gates all changes.
